claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct: newspaper as a daily or periodic printed news publication matches the intended sense.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct and ordinary for Indonesian newspaper; the Indonesian dictionary definition directly gives newspaper/daily/periodical publication.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: koran

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct and standard in Malaysian Malay for newspaper, though akhbar also has the broader meaning news/report(s).
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian Malay answer: akhbar

claim_reviews.conclusion: Needs correction: “different-common-word” is too categorical because surat kabar/surat khabar is documented as a newspaper term in both varieties. A relation such as shared-synonym-preference or different-preferred-form is safer.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No robust false-friend contrast is present. The useful learner note is that Malay akhbar can also mean news/reports, whereas Indonesian KBBI marks akhbar as Malaysian for the newspaper sense.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: The English cue and both target forms are substantively correct, but the relation “different-common-word” overstates the contrast. Indonesian koran and Malaysian Malay akhbar are valid preferred forms, while surat kabar/surat khabar is also shared and ordinary. No direct false-friend contrast is established; akhbar additionally means news/report(s) in Malay, so that nuance should be noted.
